target_customer: Enterprises, banks, government and AI teams in regulated industries that need to run applications and data in hardware-encrypted enclaves on public clouds
problem: Data in use is exposed in memory on cloud machines, and recoding applications for secure enclaves is hard, which blocks regulated workloads from moving to the cloud.
business_model: Enterprise software licensing and cloud marketplace subscriptions for a confidential computing platform
product_category: Confidential computing and enclave security software

founders.name: Ayal Yogev
founders.background_notes: Named Founder/CEO on the YC page and CEO and co-founder in the June 2021 Anjuna press release. Background not found in opened sources.

competitors.name: Fortanix
competitors.what: Runtime encryption and self-defending key management using Intel SGX enclaves
competitors.traction_then: Finalist in the 2018 RSA Conference Innovation Sandbox contest
competitors.funding_then: Series B of 23 million dollars followed in January 2019; total 31 million after it per SecurityWeek

technical_complexity.rationale: Running unmodified applications inside hardware enclaves across Intel, AMD and later other chips needed low-level systems and cryptography work on young hardware features.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integration with chip vendors and cloud marketplaces and multi-hardware support, but cloud providers and Fortanix offer overlapping enclave tooling.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Cloud providers built confidential computing options but also became Anjuna partners and marketplace channels; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: Intel SGX enclaves existed but required application changes. Fortanix was an RSA Innovation Sandbox finalist in 2018, showing enterprise interest in protecting data in use.

identity.voice_and_tone: Enterprise-ready claims about simple hardware-grade protection

branding.community_and_virality: No community or merch evidence; recognition is through industry awards listed on the company site.

brand_strength.rationale: Name shares a Goa village name with no sourced link to the product, and no brand press was found beyond awards and funding news.

outcome_analysis: Anjuna sells enclave-based confidential computing and raised a 30 million dollar Series B led by Insight Partners in 2021, bringing its total to over 42 million. It hired heavily in 2021 then cut staff in two rounds in 2022 after enterprise deals came slowly, and raised a 25 million dollar extension in 2024 on an AI focus. It remains independent and active.
notes: Total raised over 42 million at the 2021 Series B means roughly 12 million came earlier; a seed in early 2018 and a Series A in 2019 or 2020 are listed only by aggregators (Bouncewatch, Caplight, CB Insights) with conflicting dates and amounts, so they are not recorded as rounds. Aggregator totals of 58.37 million and 79 million also conflict. The 2024 extension investors were not named in opened sources. Layoffs in 2022 come from repostings of a TechCrunch article of about April 2026, one underlying account. Only one founder is confirmed by opened sources.
